questions.question: Q: How should you manage your time in the AQA 8236 written exam?

points.text: Allocate approximately 1.5 minutes per mark. Read all questions first, then start with your strongest topic. For a 6-mark question, allow about 9 minutes including planning time. Leave 5 minutes at the end for checking.

questions.question: Q: What is the PEEL structure and why is it useful?

points.text: PEEL stands for Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link. It ensures each paragraph has a clear point, is supported by specific evidence from the work, explains how the evidence supports the point, and links back to the choreographic intention or question focus.

questions.question: Q: How should you approach an annotation question?

points.text: Use precise dance terminology — not vague labels. Place labels accurately on the correct part of the diagram. Cover action, dynamics, space and relationships where relevant, and ensure each annotation is specific rather than general.

questions.question: Q: Why is it important to plan extended answers before writing?

points.text: Planning ensures your answer is structured, covers all required elements and directly addresses the command word. A brief outline prevents waffle, ensures you include evidence and keeps your answer focused on the question.

questions.question: Q: What should you check for when reviewing your answers at the end of the exam?

points.text: Check that you have answered the command word correctly, used specific dance terminology, supported points with evidence from the work, written in full sentences, and not left any questions blank.
